question: What kind of difference, if any, can coherently explain distinction?
premises: Spatial difference collapses into mutual dependence.
Mutual dependence cannot establish any real difference of place.
Only difference of intrinsic nature could coherently serve as a differentiator.
inference: If difference is to be coherent, it must be intrinsic difference of nature rather than spatial difference.
plain_english: Thus, because of mutual dependence, there is no real difference of place; only a difference of intrinsic nature would fit as a true differentiator.
